recipes.title: Cheese Ball
ingredients: 1/2 glass Old English Cheddar or Pineapple Cheese
About 1 c. chopped pecans, for rolling (best guess)
2 to 3 tbsp. parsley flakes, for rolling (best guess)
steps: Add onion salt and garlic salt to the cheeses and mash with a fork. Mix well.
Roll into two balls, about baseball size.
Roll in chopped pecans and parsley flakes and put in a 20 oz. canister.
Refrigerate overnight.
notes: Family thinks this page came from a church recipe collection, with Edi Dobbins as the contributor.
Two versions: one made with Old English Cheddar, one with Pineapple Cheese. Family guess is that event batches were a mix of both.
Card says the balls can be frozen ahead and stored in a Kracker Keeper.
"Old English" is Kraft's sharp cheese spread, sold in a small glass jar, hence "1/2 glass."
flags: The last line reads "(Six can be frozen ahead and stored in Kracker Keeper)." Possibly means six balls (three batches) made ahead and frozen for an event. That reading isn't confirmed.
"Put in refrigerator overnight" was typed above "Canister" on the card. Steps put back in order.

No amounts on the card for the salts, pecans, or parsley. The amounts listed are best guesses from similar vintage cheese ball recipes. Start low on the salts, since the blue cheese and Old English are already salty, and taste before rolling.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Bread
steps: Beat sugar, pumpkin and oil well.
Add flour sifted with salt, baking soda and cloves. The batter will be rather stiff.
Add nuts and prunes.
Put in 3 greased 9x5 loaf pans (best guess; card just says loaf pans) and bake at 350° for about 1-1/2 hours.
notes: "1 large can" pumpkin was usually the 29 oz can.
flags: Number of loaf pans isn't stated. Best guess is three 9x5 pans: similar recipes with 3 to 3-1/2 cups flour and about 2 cups pumpkin make two loaves in 1-1/2 hours, and this one is about half again bigger, with prunes and nuts on top. Fill pans about 2/3 full.

Same sheet as the Cheese Ball: this recipe is on one side and the Cheese Ball on the other. The "(Continued)" at the bottom points to the Cheese Ball side, so this recipe is complete. The Edi Dobbins stamp on the Cheese Ball side may cover this recipe too.

recipes.title: Date Bread or Pudding (partial)

photos.label: Top of the Pumpkin Bread page
Close-up of the torn top edge showing "1 c. sugar"

ingredients: 1 c. sugar (last ingredient line; the rest is on an earlier sheet)
steps: Pour boiling water over dates and soda. Cool before combining with other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
notes: Delicious served with whipped cream as a dessert, or cook in a loaf pan and slice as a bread. Ideal for buffets.
flags: Only the end of this recipe is on this sheet (the Pumpkin Bread / Cheese Ball sheet). The title and ingredients must be on an earlier sheet in the box.
Second number in the bake time is under the tear. Most likely 60.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
steps: Mix all dry ingredients except the sugar.
Beat butter, adding sugar while beating. Add eggs.
Add the flour mixture, then the bananas.
Heat oven to 350°. Grease a loaf pan and pour in the batter.
Bake for 1 hour.
notes: Tammy's own recipe card, added to Grandma's box.
"(Overly Ripe)" was added later in a different blue pen, so someone baked from this card and adjusted it.
flags: A few words after "Bananas" are scribbled out.
"Pour" runs off the edge of the card and was filled in.

recipes.title: Holiday Wreaths
ingredients: 1 package (10 oz., about 40) regular marshmallows, or 4 cups miniature marshmallows
6 cups corn flakes or frosted flakes cereal
steps: Melt the margarine in a large saucepan over low heat. Add the marshmallows and stir until fully melted and smooth. Take off the heat and stir in the green coloring.
Stir in the cereal until it's evenly coated.
While the mixture is still warm, scoop it out in 1/4-cup portions with a measuring cup sprayed with cooking spray. With greased fingers, quickly shape each into a small wreath.
Stick on cinnamon candies with a dab of frosting. Store in a single layer in an airtight container.
notes: Microwave option: heat the margarine and marshmallows on high about 2 minutes, stir, then 1 minute more. Stir smooth, add the coloring, and continue from step 2.
One large wreath: press the warm mixture into a greased 5-1/2 cup ring mold, or shape a ring on a serving plate. Unmold, dot with candies, and slice to serve.
Paste food coloring gives the best green, and fresh marshmallows work best.
Original is a printout from Kellogg's recipe site, dated 2011. Directions here are reworded; the printout photo isn't posted since it's Kellogg's page.

recipes.title: Melting Moments
ingredients: Frosting: red coloring and 1/8 tsp. vanilla
Frosting: green coloring and a few drops peppermint
steps: Cream the butter and powdered sugar. Blend in the flour, kneading with your hands as the dough gets too stiff.
Roll the dough into long rolls about as big around as a quarter. Wrap in wax paper or foil.
Chill in the refrigerator about 2 hours.
Unwrap and slice into thin slices. Bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 300° for about 20 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool.
Frosting: beat the butter, powdered sugar and milk until smooth. Divide into 3 parts: tint one red with the vanilla, one green with the peppermint, and leave one white with the almond.
Put the cookies together in pairs with the frosting.
notes: Grandma Sharp's handwriting. She spells it "untill," which helps spot her other cards.
Written on the card: "good, nice for Christmas."
Red, green and white frosting makes these a Christmas cookie tray.
Card is kept in a plastic sleeve.
The original newspaper clipping for this recipe is also in the box (No. 040).
flags: The bake time reads "about 20 min" with the 20 written over another word. 20 minutes fits a slow 300° oven and thin slices.
Sugar is listed beside "cream butter" but not named in the step. Creaming it with the butter is the usual method.

recipes.title: Chewy Brownie Cookies
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups firmly packed light brown sugar
2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chips (12 oz. pkg.)
steps: Heat the oven to 375°. Lay out sheets of foil on the counter for cooling.
Beat the shortening, brown sugar, water and vanilla on medium speed until well blended. Beat in the eggs.
In another bowl, mix the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt. Mix into the creamed mixture on low speed just until combined. Stir in the chocolate chips.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough 2 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake one sheet at a time for 7 to 9 minutes, just until set. Don't overbake; they should still look soft. Cool 2 minutes on the sheet, then move to the foil to finish cooling.
notes: Original is a recipe cut from a Crisco package. Directions here are reworded; the clipping photo isn't posted since it's Crisco's printed recipe.

recipes.title: Butter Cream Frosting
ingredients: 1/4 cup milk, plus a few drops if needed
1/3 cup soft butter or margarine (2/3 stick)
steps: Combine everything in a mixing bowl.
Beat with an electric mixer or a heavy spoon until smooth and creamy, scraping the bowl often.
If it's too stiff to spread easily, beat in a few drops of milk.
notes: Written by Tammy on a printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, signed "Recipe from: Tammy Jones."
Tammy thinks this frosting went with the cookie class, paired with Steve's dough (No. 010).
Pairs naturally with the cake cards in the box.
flags: One word at the start is scribbled out before "In a mixing bowl."
"Serves" is left blank. A pound of powdered sugar usually frosts a 9x13 or a two-layer 8-inch cake.

recipes.title: Old Time Cottage Cheese Cookies
recipes.yield: 6 or more dozen (end of number is stained)
steps: Cream together the butter, sugars, vanilla, eggs, cottage cheese and cocoa. Mix well and set aside.
Mix the baking powder, soda and flour. Add to the creamed mixture, add the nuts, and stir well.
Chill the dough in the freezer until firm enough to roll, about 1 hour (best guess).
Preheat the oven to 350° and lightly grease a cookie sheet.
Roll the dough into walnut-sized balls, then roll in powdered sugar. Place on the cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes (best guess; time is stained).
notes: Tammy's, on her Vision "thought pad" notepad paper.
"Add nuts" was squeezed into the margin beside the mixing step.
Rolled in powdered sugar, these bake up like chocolate crinkle cookies.
A recipe online matches this one almost exactly at half size (same flour, cocoa, cottage cheese, eggs, vanilla, leaveners and nuts), which backs up the readings above.
flags: The white sugar amount is under a stain. The math on the back (3/4 + 3/4 = 1-1/2 cup) points to 3/4 cup each of white and brown sugar, and a nearly identical online recipe uses about the same total.
Bake time is stained; only a 1 survives. Similar recipes bake 10 minutes at 350°, so 10 minutes is the best guess.
Yield reads "makes 6 to" and the rest is stained.
Chill time isn't stated. Similar recipes chill 1 hour to overnight.
"67 1/4" written on the back doesn't appear to be part of the recipe.
recipes.time: Chill about 1 hr · Bake about 10 min

recipes.title: Cookie Dough for Cookie Classes
steps: Let the butter soften. Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk the flour and salt together, then mix them in on low just until the dough comes together.
Divide the dough in half, flatten each into a disc, wrap, and chill about 1 hour, until firm.
Heat the oven to 350°. Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick on a lightly floured counter and cut into shapes.
Place 1 inch apart on an ungreased or parchment-lined cookie sheet. If the cut-outs get soft, chill the sheet 10 minutes so they hold their shape.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges just start to turn golden. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then move to a rack.
Cool completely, then decorate with the Butter Cream Frosting (No. 008).
notes: Steve Jones is William's dad. Tammy was likely taking a cookie class, needed a dough recipe, and got this one from Steve.
Tammy thinks it was paired with her Butter Cream Frosting (No. 008) for the class.
Same printed "Here's what's cookin'" card style as Tammy's Butter Cream Frosting.
flags: Title is faint and runs off the top corner. It reads like "Cookie dough for cookie classes."

The card lists ingredients only. These directions are a best guess for a roll-and-cut butter cookie, written to go with the class frosting. If Steve or Tammy remembers how it was done, theirs replaces this.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 375°.
Cream the shortening, both sugars, vanilla, water and eggs until light and fluffy.
Mix the flour, soda and salt, and add to the creamed mixture.
Stir in the chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by rounded teaspoons onto a cookie sheet (best guess; the card doesn't say).
Bake about 10 minutes, or until golden brown.
notes: Grandma Sharp's handwriting, confirmed by Tammy. Like her Melting Moments card, she spells it "untill."
Printed card with a little girl, kitten and puppy at a tea table, and an Israeli proverb about a shared table ending arguments.
Card is kept in a plastic sleeve.

recipes.title: No Bake Cookies
steps: Melt the chips and peanut butter together and mix.
Put the noodles and marshmallows in a bowl. Pour the melted mixture over them and mix. Don't let the marshmallows melt.
Drop by teaspoons onto a cookie sheet and let cool until set.
notes: Two hands on this card: Tammy thinks the printed title is her mom's writing, and the cursive recipe below is likely Grandma Sharp's. The recipe uses Grandma's habit of bracketing ingredients with an instruction beside them, and "+" for "and."
This is the classic "haystacks" candy-cookie.
"Choc chips or" and the marshmallow line were added later in lighter pencil, so the original version was butterscotch and noodles only.
flags: No marshmallow amount. Haystack recipes that add them usually use about 1 to 2 cups of miniatures.
Package and can sizes have changed over the years. A standard bag of chips is 10 to 11 oz, and a large can of chow mein noodles is about 5 oz.

recipes.title: Irresistible Peanut Butter Cookies
ingredients: 1-1/4 cups firmly packed light brown sugar
steps: Heat the oven to 375°. Lay out sheets of foil on the counter for cooling.
Beat the peanut butter, shortening, brown sugar, milk and vanilla on medium speed until well blended. Beat in the egg just until combined.
Mix the flour, salt and baking soda, and add to the creamed mixture on low speed just until blended.
Drop heaping teaspoons of dough 2 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet. Press lightly with a fork in a crisscross pattern.
Bake 7 to 8 minutes, until set and just starting to brown. Cool 2 minutes on the sheet, then move to the foil to finish cooling.
notes: Original is a recipe cut from a Crisco package, from the same series as the Chewy Brownie Cookies (No. 007). Directions here are reworded; the clipping photo isn't posted.
Tip printed on the card: to use Crisco in place of 1 cup butter or margarine, use 1 cup Crisco plus 6 teaspoons water.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.time: Bake 8 to 10 min (chewy) or 11 to 13 min (crisp)
ingredients: 1-1/4 cups firmly packed light brown sugar
1 cup coarsely chopped pecans (optional; if left out, add another 1/2 cup chips)
steps: Heat the oven to 375°. Lay out sheets of foil on the counter for cooling.
Beat the shortening, brown sugar, milk and vanilla on medium speed until well blended. Beat in the egg.
Mix the flour, salt and baking soda, and mix into the creamed mixture just until combined. Stir in the chips and pecans.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough 3 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake one sheet at a time: 8 to 10 minutes for chewy cookies, or 11 to 13 minutes for crisp. Don't overbake. Cool 2 minutes on the sheet, then move to the foil.
notes: Original is a recipe cut from a Crisco package, card 13 in the same series as No. 007 and No. 013. Directions here are reworded; the clipping photo isn't posted.
Compare with Grandma Sharp's own Chocolate Chip Cookies (No. 011).

recipes.title: Rolled Sugar Cookies
recipes.time: Chill 2 hr to overnight · Bake about 10 min
steps: Cream the margarine, sugar, vanilla and egg until light and fluffy.
Add the flour and baking powder and blend well.
Chill the dough 2 hours or overnight.
Roll out on a lightly floured counter to 1/8 inch thick and cut with cookie cutters.
Bake on an ungreased baking sheet at 375° until lightly browned, about 10 minutes. Cool before storing.
notes: Clipped from a typed newsletter with a Christmas bell drawing. The other side reports on the 1989 "Fun In The Sun" diabetes camp at Lake Coeur d'Alene, which dates the clipping to about late 1989.
A slice-and-bake version of the same dough, with a Sugar Twin option, is No. 016.
Printed exchange info: 2 cookies = 1/2 starch and 1/2 fat exchange.
Directions reworded from the clipping.

recipes.title: Sugar Cookies (For Anyone or Diabetics)
ingredients: 1/2 cup sugar, or 1/4 cup sugar plus 1/4 cup Sugar Twin
steps: Cream the margarine, sugar, vanilla and egg until light and fluffy. Blend in the flour and baking powder.
Shape the dough into a log about 10 inches long and 2 inches thick. Wrap in wax paper or foil and chill about 2 hours.
Slice 1/8 inch thick with a knife.
Bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 375° for 10 minutes. Cool before storing, then decorate with sprinkles or frosting.
notes: Same dough as the Rolled Sugar Cookies (No. 015), made as slice-and-bake instead of rolled and cut, with a Sugar Twin option to cut the sugar in half.
Directions reworded from the clipping.
flags: A 10-inch log cut 1/8 inch thick gives far more than 3 dozen. Either the slices were meant to be thicker or the yield is understated.

recipes.title: Crisp Peanut Butter Sandwich Cookies
ingredients: Peanut butter, for the filling (amount not given)
steps: Cream the shortening, sugar and vanilla. Add the egg and mix well.
Sift the flour, salt and soda together and stir into the creamed mixture.
Divide the dough in half. On waxed paper, roll each half into a log 1-1/2 inches across. Wrap and chill overnight; the dough has to be firm to slice.
Slice one log at a time, thin, with a sharp knife. Bake 1 inch apart on an ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for about 10 minutes.
When cool, spread peanut butter on the bottom of half the cookies, top with the rest, bottom side down, and press gently.
notes: The spelling "cooky" was common in newspaper recipes of the 1950s and '60s, so this clipping may be one of the older ones.
The dough itself has no peanut butter; it's all in the filling.
Directions reworded from the clipping.
flags: No amount for the peanut butter filling. About 3/4 to 1 cup should fill 2 dozen sandwiches.

recipes.title: No-Bake Cookie Balls
steps: Bring the sugar, cocoa and milk to a boil in a saucepan and boil 1 minute.
Take off the heat and stir in the butter, peanut butter, vanilla and oats.
Roll into balls. Store at room temperature.
notes: The classic chocolate-oatmeal no-bake, shaped into balls here instead of dropped. Compare with the haystack-style No Bake Cookies (No. 012).
Directions reworded from the clipping.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Ice Box Cookies
steps: Mix the ingredients in the order listed.
Roll into logs and chill until firm, then slice.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
notes: Written at the top: "Very good (Margaret)." "Ice box" is the old name for slice-and-bake cookies chilled in the refrigerator.
Family doesn't know Margaret; probably someone from church.
flags: "Slice" and the "min" after the bake time run off the right edge of the card.

recipes.title: Zucchini-Nut Cookies
steps: Cream the shortening and both sugars.
Add the grated zucchini.
Mix the flour, soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt, and add.
Stir in the chopped nuts.
Drop onto a greased baking tin and bake at 325° for 10 minutes.
notes: Circled at the top: "From Fran Harmon."
Family doesn't know Fran; probably someone from church.
flags: There's no egg in this recipe; the zucchini supplies the moisture. That's as written, not a missed line.
Name reads "Harmon" or "Harman."

recipes.title: Applesauce Drop Cookies
steps: Cream the shortening and sugar together. Add the egg.
Mix the flour, soda, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Add the flour mixture and applesauce to the creamed mixture alternately.
Stir in the raisins and nuts last.
Drop and bake at 400° for about 15 minutes.
flags: The writing is faint. The first line reads as 1/2 cup shortening.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Cookies
steps: Cream the margarine and sugar. Beat in the pumpkin and egg.
Stir the flour, soda, cinnamon and salt into the creamed mixture.
Stir in the raisins and nuts, if using.
Drop onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
notes: Tammy thinks this is her grandmother's handwriting.
Same printed "Here's what's cookin'" card series as Tammy's frosting and Steve's dough cards, in green.
flags: Raisins and nuts both have question marks after them, so the writer seems to have treated them as optional. No amount for the nuts; about 1/2 cup is typical.

recipes.title: Apple Cookies (No Bake)
steps: Put the apples, margarine, sugar and salt in a pan. Bring to a boil and cook for 1 1/2 minutes.
Add the oatmeal, nuts and vanilla and mix well.
Drop onto wax paper and chill 2 to 3 hours.
Roll in powdered sugar. Enjoy!
notes: Tammy's Apple Oat Cookies card (No. 024) is her copy of this same recipe.
flags: A word is scribbled out just before "Pd. sugar" on the last line.

recipes.title: Apple Oat Cookies
steps: Bring the apples, margarine, sugar and salt to a boil and cook for 1 1/2 minutes.
Then add the oats and vanilla and mix well.
Drop a spoonful at a time onto wax paper and chill for 2 to 3 hours.
After they're chilled, sprinkle powdered sugar over the top if you like. Hope you enjoy!
notes: Tammy's version of No. 023. It leaves out the nuts and sprinkles the sugar on top instead of rolling.
flags: This card says 1 tablespoon of vanilla; the older card (No. 023) and similar no-bake apple cookie recipes online all use 1 teaspoon, so the tablespoon is probably a slip.

recipes.title: Fudge-Nut Cookies
steps: Cream the margarine and sugar.
Add the eggs, cottage cheese and vanilla and mix well.
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, soda and salt together and add to the creamed mixture, then add the nuts.
Cover and chill several hours or overnight.
Roll into walnut-sized balls and roll in powdered sugar.
Place on a cookie sheet and bake at 375° for about 10 to 12 minutes.
notes: The dough can also be kept in the refrigerator for 2 or 3 days and baked as wanted.
A chocolate cousin of the Old Time Cottage Cheese Cookies (No. 009).

recipes.title: Kim's Country Cookies (Ginger Snaps)
steps: Beat together the oil, molasses, sugar and egg.
Add the flour, soda, salt and spices and mix well. Stir in the raisins.
Chill.
Roll into balls, then roll in sugar and place on a cookie sheet.
Bake 8 minutes in a 350° oven.
notes: Written in Grandma Sharp's handwriting, filed under Tammy's maiden name, Brooks. Tammy liked making these and made them for church.
"Ginger Snaps" is written in the corner next to the name. Compare the clipped Ginger Snaps recipe (No. 031), which uses shortening instead of oil.
Card has the little cook-with-ice-cream picture and the Proverbs line at the bottom.
flags: The raisin line might say "Craisins." Ocean Spray's Craisins only reached stores in the mid-1990s, so if the card is older than that it's plain raisins.

recipes.title: Apple Oatmeal Cookie
steps: Cream the shortening, brown sugar and vanilla. Beat in the eggs.
Sift the flour, salt, baking powder, soda and cinnamon together and stir into the creamed mixture.
Add the oatmeal, raisins, walnuts and chopped apples.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
notes: Pasted on a lined card with "Apple Oatmeal Cookies" handwritten down the side.
The lines of the printed directions are a little jumbled on the clipping; the steps above put them back in order.

recipes.title: Sugar Cookies
steps: Mix all ingredients.
Form into balls and flatten with a fork or the bottom of a glass.
Sprinkle with sugar before baking, if desired.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 350°.
notes: Signed and dated at the top: Leona Kern, March 1979.
With 9 cups of flour this makes a lot of cookies; halving it works fine.

recipes.title: Soft Oatmeal Cookies
steps: Cream the shortening, brown sugar and eggs until light and fluffy. Stir in the buttermilk.
Sift the flour, salt, baking powder, soda and spices together and stir into the creamed mixture.
Add the oats, raisins and nuts and mix well.
Drop by tablespoonfuls 2 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cool thoroughly, then store in a tightly covered container.
notes: Pasted in two pieces on a lined card titled "Soft oatmeal Cookies" by hand.
flags: The clipping prints "1/2 cup chopped nuts" twice in a row. That's almost certainly a newspaper typo, so it's listed once here.

recipes.title: Sour Cream Drop Cookies
steps: Cream the brown sugar, shortening and eggs together.
Mix the salt, nutmeg, flour, soda and baking powder, and add to the creamed mixture along with the sour cream.
Add nuts, raisins, chips or coconut if you like.
Drop onto a cookie sheet and bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
notes: Title on the card is spelled "Soor Cream."
A published vintage Sour Cream Cookies recipe matches this card almost exactly, including 4 tsp. baking powder and 15 minutes in a hot oven, so the card reads right as written.

recipes.title: Ginger Snaps
ingredients: 1/2 tsp. each cloves, salt, ginger and cinnamon
steps: Cream the shortening and sugar. Add the egg and molasses and beat well.
Sift the flour with the salt, soda and spices and fold in.
Chill the dough several hours or overnight.
Roll into small balls about the size of walnuts and roll in granulated sugar. Don't flatten.
Bake at 375° for about 10 minutes. Do not overbake.
notes: Close relative of Kim's Country Cookies (No. 026), which uses oil and raisins.

recipes.title: "Good" Famous Oatmeal Cookies
steps: Mix the shortening, brown sugar and white sugar.
Add the egg, water and vanilla and mix.
Add the flour, salt and soda and mix, then add the oatmeal.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
notes: "Good" is written and underlined in the corner, a nice seal of approval.
For variety the card suggests nuts, chips, coconut or raisins.

recipes.title: Orange Drop Cookies
ingredients: Optional: chips, nuts, orange juice and rind, coconut, oatmeal
steps: Mix the wet ingredients, then the dry ingredients, and combine.
Add any of the extras you like.
Drop onto a cookie sheet and bake in a 400° oven.
notes: The orange comes from the optional orange juice and rind; the base dough is plain.
flags: No baking time on the card. Similar vintage Orange Drop Cookie recipes bake 8 to 10 minutes at 400°.

recipes.title: Brownies

photos.label: Clipping (Brownies, Mint Patties and Fudge together)

steps: Cream the margarine and sugar; stir in the corn syrup and vanilla.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Combine the flour and cocoa and stir into the creamed mixture. Add the nuts.
Turn into a greased 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes, or until a wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack and cut into squares.
notes: Shares one long clipping with Chocolate Mint Patties (No. 035) and Rocky Road Fudge (No. 036).
flags: The sugar amount is smudged; it reads as 3/4 cup.

recipes.title: Chocolate Mint Patties

photos.label: Clipping (Brownies, Mint Patties and Fudge together)

steps: Combine the butter, corn syrup and peppermint extract in a large mixer bowl.
Sift the powdered sugar and cocoa together.
Gradually add about 2 cups of the sugar mixture to the butter mixture, beating until well blended.
Work in the rest of the sugar mixture with a wooden spoon, then knead with your hands until smooth.
Shape into balls using about 1 teaspoon for each, and flatten into round patties.
Store in tightly covered containers in a cool place or the refrigerator.
notes: No cooking needed. Same clipping as Brownies (No. 034).

recipes.title: Rocky Road Fudge

photos.label: Full clipping (with Brownies and Mint Patties)

steps: In a 2-quart saucepan, melt the butter over low heat; stir in the cocoa, corn syrup, water and vanilla.
Remove from heat and gradually add the powdered sugar, stirring until well blended.
Stir in the marshmallows and nuts.
Turn into a buttered 8-inch square pan. Cover and refrigerate until firm.
Cut into squares.
notes: Same clipping as Brownies (No. 034).

recipes.title: Peanutbutter Cookies
steps: Cream the peanut butter, shortening, sugar and brown sugar together in a bowl.
Add the boiling water, then add the baking mix and mix.
Make 1-inch balls and flatten with a fork dipped in sugar in a criss-cross pattern.
Bake at 400° for 9 to 11 minutes.
notes: A shortcut version made with biscuit mix (like Bisquick).

recipes.title: Ginger Snaps (Vicky's)
steps: Mix the sugar, butter, egg and molasses.
Mix the spices, salt, soda and flour, then combine and mix well.
Make little balls and roll in sugar.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
notes: Marked "(Vicky) good" at the top. Vicky is Tammy's mother and Grandma Sharp's daughter, so this is Grandma's note that it's her daughter's recipe, and a good one.
The third ginger snap recipe in the box, with Kim's Country Cookies (No. 026) and the clipping (No. 031). This one uses butter and only 2 tablespoons of molasses.

recipes.title: Cream Cookies
steps: Dissolve the soda and baking powder in the milk. (This is where the card ends; the rest is filled in from similar old recipes.)
Cream the shortening and sugar, then beat in the eggs and lemon extract.
Add the milk mixture alternately with the flour and salt, mixing well. The dough will be stiff.
Roll out on a floured board about 1/4 inch thick and cut with a cookie cutter, or drop by spoonfuls and flatten with a sugared glass.
Bake on a greased cookie sheet at 350° for about 8 to 12 minutes, until the centers spring back.
notes: The back of the card is blank; the card only gives the first step.
flags: Steps 2 to 5 are a best guess based on similar old-fashioned cream cookie recipes, not the card. With 6 cups of flour this is a stiff dough that most versions roll and cut.

recipes.title: Melting Moments (with Pastel Frosting)
ingredients: Pastel Frosting: 1/4 cup butter, 2 cups powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon milk
1/8 teaspoon vanilla, a few drops each peppermint and almond extract
steps: Cream the butter and blend in the sugar. Work in the flour, kneading with your hands once the dough gets too stiff to stir.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Divide the dough in half and roll out on a lightly floured board to 1/8 inch thick.
Cut out circles about the size of a quarter (the "hole" from a doughnut cutter works).
Bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 300° for about 20 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool.

For the frosting, blend the butter, powdered sugar and milk until smooth and divide into three parts: tint one pink and flavor with vanilla, tint one green and flavor with peppermint, and leave one white and flavor with almond.
Put the cookies together in pairs with the frosting.
notes: The top of the clipping is torn, but the title is Melting Moments.
This is the same recipe as Grandma Sharp's Melting Moments card (No. 006), so this clipping is probably where she copied it from.

recipes.title: Snowballs
steps: Mix the oleo, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Mix the flour and salt, then combine with the butter mixture and add the nuts.
Roll into 1-inch balls and place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes, until set but not brown.
While warm, roll in powdered sugar. Cool, then roll in sugar again.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles
steps: Mix the shortening, sugar and eggs.
Sift the flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt.
Combine, roll into balls and roll in a cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
notes: Faint pencil, in a plastic sleeve.

recipes.title: Rich Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.format: Printed recipe card (C and H Sugar)
ingredients: 1/2 cup golden brown sugar, firmly packed
1/2 teaspoon each baking powder and salt
steps: Cream together the shortening, butter, peanut butter and sugars. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Combine the flour, soda, baking powder and salt; stir into the creamed mixture and mix well.
Chill.
With floured hands, shape the soft dough into 1-inch balls. Place on a greased cookie sheet and flatten with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
notes: A C and H Sugar promotional card.

recipes.title: Basic Drop Dough
ingredients: Colored sugar or candies, for decorating (optional)
steps: Mix the margarine and brown sugar.
Add the egg and vanilla.
Add the flour and baking powder and blend.
Drop by large teaspoonfuls onto a baking sheet.
Decorate with colored sugar or candies.
Bake in a 350° oven for 10 minutes.
notes: Variation: add chocolate chips and drop.
flags: The flour amount was changed in blue ink and looks like 1 1/2 cups.

recipes.title: Chocolate Dream Bars
recipes.format: Newspaper cartoon recipe, front and back
steps: Boil the first 5 ingredients for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the last 3 ingredients and stir until thick.
Spoon onto wax paper and cut into squares. Yum!
notes: A hand-drawn, kids-style picture recipe. Basically the classic no-bake cookie (compare No. 012) spread out and cut into bars.
flags: The oatmeal amount is shown as three 1-cup measuring cups split across the front and back, so it reads as 3 cups.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cake
ingredients: 1/2 pkg. chocolate chips, plus more for the top
steps: Mix the boiling water and oats and let sit 10 minutes.
Add the brown sugar, sugar and margarine and stir until the margarine melts.
Add the eggs.
Mix the flour, soda, salt and cocoa and add to the batter. Add 1/2 package of chocolate chips.
Pour into a 9x13 pan and sprinkle chips and nuts on top.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
notes: Marked "(no frosting)": the chips and nuts on top take its place.
Credited to Ann Caldwell at the top of the card.
flags: The back turned up loose in a later batch; matched to this card by handwriting and the chips-and-nuts topping.

recipes.title: Easy Chocolate Frosting
steps: Melt the chocolate and butter over hot water.
Blend the sugar, salt, milk and vanilla.
Add the hot chocolate mixture and mix well.
Let stand, stirring occasionally, until it's the right consistency to spread on cake.
notes: Pasted on one card with Quick Coconut Topping (No. 048).
flags: The yield is cut off at the bottom of the clipping.

recipes.title: Quick Coconut Topping
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan and stir in the brown sugar and evaporated milk.
Heat just to a boil, stirring.
Remove from heat and add the coconut and nuts.
notes: Pasted on one card with Easy Chocolate Frosting (No. 047). Compare the Broiler Coconut Topping card (No. 061).

recipes.title: Seven Minute Frosting
steps: Combine everything but the vanilla in the top of a double boiler.
Beat over boiling water for seven minutes, until it stands in peaks.
Cool and add the vanilla.
notes: Faint pencil, in a plastic sleeve.

recipes.title: Fluffy Cocoa Frosting
steps: Mix the cocoa and powdered sugar.
Cream the butter with part of the sugar mixture.
Add the vanilla to half of the milk and add it.
Add the rest of the sugar mixture and milk and beat to the consistency you want. Use more milk if needed.
flags: The card's vanilla looks like a capital T, but matching online Fluffy Cocoa Frosting recipes (same cocoa, sugar, butter and evaporated milk) all use 1 teaspoon, so that's listed here.

recipes.title: Sugarless Raisin Cake
steps: Boil the water, oil, raisins, cinnamon and allspice for 3 minutes. Let cool.
Mix the sweetener, 2 tsp. water, baking powder, salt and soda until dissolved, and add to the beaten eggs.
Combine with the cooled raisin mixture.
Add the flour, then the nuts.
Spread in a greased pan and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
notes: Can also be dropped as cookies and baked at 350° for about 7 minutes.
Someone wrote "Cheeseburger" sideways down the right edge, no idea why.
A diabetic-friendly recipe, like the others from the diabetes camp newsletter.
flags: The flour number was written over; it looks like 2 cups.
No amount for the nuts and no pan size.

recipes.title: Apple Cake Pie
steps: Put the apples in the bottom of a pie tin and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, melted butter, egg and milk in a dish and pour over the apples.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes, until golden brown. (The card gives no oven time; this comes from similar crustless apple pie recipes.)
Serve warm or cold with a thin custard sauce or any kind of topping.
notes: Marked "Good." From Elsie Kull.
flags: The bake time and temperature aren't on the card. Similar Swedish/crustless apple pies bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

recipes.title: Boston Cream Pie
recipes.format: Printed recipe card, front and back
ingredients: Custard: 1/2 c. sugar, 3 T. flour, pinch of salt, 1 c. milk, 2 eggs, 2 T. butter, 1 tsp. vanilla
Glaze: 2 tsp. butter, chocolate chips, 1/2 c. powdered sugar, about 1 tbsp. boiling water
steps: Prepare the cake mix and bake in an 8-inch round pan. Cool, then split into two layers.
For the custard, mix the sugar, flour and salt and stir in the milk. Cook until it thickens.
Beat the eggs and blend in about half of the hot pudding, then stir it all back into the pan.
Cook, stirring, about 2 minutes until very thick. Remove from heat and stir in the butter and vanilla. Cover and chill.
Put the layers together with the custard filling.
For the glaze, melt the butter and chips, stir in the powdered sugar and about 1 tbsp. boiling water to make it spreadable. Spread over the top.
notes: Shortcut: use 1 package of regular cook-type vanilla pudding instead, but with only 1 1/2 cups milk.
flags: No amount for the chocolate chips in the glaze; about 1/2 cup is typical.

recipes.title: Apricot Cake
recipes.format: Printed recipe card, front and back
steps: Pour the fruit and juice into a 9x13 pan.
Sprinkle the dry cake mix on top.
Put the coconut, nuts and cinnamon on the cake mix.
Drizzle the margarine on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
notes: A dump cake. The card stock is dated 1986.

recipes.title: Fruit Cocktail Torte (Cake)
ingredients: Topping: 1 c. brown sugar, 1/2 c. nuts
steps: Mix everything in one bowl and put in a 12x8 pan.
Sprinkle the top with the brown sugar and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream or ice cream.
notes: The typed copy adds: "Sounds weird with no shortening but this is right."

recipes.title: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
ingredients: 1 can (20 oz.) sliced pineapple in juice, drained, juice saved
Oil and eggs as called for on the cake mix
steps: Heat the oven to 350°. Melt the butter in a 13x9 pan in the oven.
Sprinkle the brown sugar evenly over the butter. Arrange the pineapple and cherries on top and press gently.
Add water to the pineapple juice to make 1 1/4 cups.
Make the cake batter as the package says, but use the pineapple juice mixture instead of water. Pour over the fruit.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Immediately turn the pan upside down onto a heatproof plate and leave the pan over the cake 1 minute. Serve warm or cool.
notes: High altitude (3500–6500 ft): grease and flour the pan, stir 3 Tbsp flour into the dry mix, and bake 45 to 50 minutes.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pudding Cake
steps: Combine all ingredients in a mixing bowl and beat 3 minutes.
Pour into a lightly oiled 3-quart ring mold or a cheesecake pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes in the pan.
Serve warm with a sprinkle of powdered sugar or a spoonful of vanilla yogurt.
notes: From a diabetic recipe sheet: "for occasional use." Exchanges per slice: 1 starch/bread, 1 fat.

recipes.title: Popcorn Cake
steps: Melt the marshmallows, oil and margarine together.
Pour over the popcorn and add M&M's and peanuts if you like.
Press into a buttered angel food cake pan or a buttered 9x13 pan.
notes: Written on a Spokane towing company message slip, with "Pop Corn Cake" on the back.

recipes.title: Pound Cake
steps: Cream the butter and sugar.
Add the eggs one at a time.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt and add.
Put in a cold oven, then bake 1 hour at 350°.
notes: "Sugar box of flour" means refill the empty 1 lb. sugar box with flour, about 3 1/2 cups.
A cold-oven pound cake: the oven heats up with the cake inside.
flags: No pan on the card; a greased and floured tube or Bundt pan is typical.

recipes.title: Classic Gingerbread
steps: Sift the dry ingredients and set aside.
Cream the shortening and sugar. Add the egg and beat until light and fluffy. Beat in the molasses.
Stir in the dry ingredients alternately with the hot water, mixing just until smooth.
Turn into a greased 9-inch square pan and bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes.
Cut in squares and serve warm or cold, with whipped cream if you like.

recipes.title: Broiler Coconut Topping
steps: Blend everything and spoon on top of the cake.
Place under the broiler 2 to 3 minutes, until bubbly and toasted.
notes: Probably the topping for the Oatmeal Cake (No. 062), which says "topping on."

recipes.title: Oatmeal Cake
steps: Combine the oats and boiling water and let sit 20 minutes.
Cream the shortening, sugar and brown sugar.
Beat the eggs and add.
Sift the flour, soda, salt and cinnamon and add to the creamed mixture.
Stir in the oatmeal.
Pour into a pan and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
notes: Marked "good." From Mrs. Anna Heath.
"Topping on" is circled in the corner. The Broiler Coconut Topping (No. 061) is the classic topping for this cake.
flags: No pan size; a 9x13 is typical.

recipes.title: Fantasy Fudge
steps: Combine the sugar, margarine and evaporated milk in a heavy pan. Bring to a full boil, stirring.
Boil 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring. Remove from heat.
Add the chocolate chips and stir until melted.
Add the marshmallow creme, nuts and vanilla and beat until well blended.
Pour onto a cookie sheet or into a 13x9 pan. Cool at room temperature, then cut.
notes: The classic marshmallow-creme fudge. The card has the girl-with-teapot picture and an Israeli proverb at the bottom.

recipes.title: English Toffee
steps: Combine the sugar, water and butter in a heavy saucepan.
Cook to 300° (hard crack stage), stirring constantly.
Add the vanilla and pour into a 9x9 pan.
Lay the chocolate bars on top and spread them evenly as they melt.
While still warm, sprinkle the chopped nuts over the top.
Cool thoroughly and break into pieces.
notes: Signed "SW" at the bottom of the back. Probably a past member of the family's church.
flags: The chocolate reads "4 7/8 oz. bars." It could mean four 7/8-oz. bars or bars totaling about 4 7/8 oz.; about 4 to 5 oz. of milk chocolate covers a 9x9 pan.

recipes.title: Fudge
steps: Mix the sugar, cocoa, milk and salt and boil until soft ball stage (about 234°).
Remove from the fire and add the butter, vanilla and nuts.
Beat until thick, pour into a buttered pan and cut into squares.
notes: Old-fashioned cooked cocoa fudge, no thermometer needed if you use the cold-water test.
flags: The cocoa amount is faint; it looks like 1/4 cup, though many versions use 1/2 cup.

recipes.title: Sister Mabel's Caramel Corn
ingredients: 2 cups light brown sugar, firmly packed
steps: In a 2 1/2-quart saucepan, combine the brown sugar, corn syrup, butter, cream of tartar and salt.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring. Stirring constantly, boil rapidly to the hard-ball stage, 260° (about 5 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in the baking soda quickly but thoroughly.
Pour at once over the popcorn in a large roasting or baking pan and stir gently until coated.
Bake at 200° for 1 hour, stirring 2 or 3 times.
Turn out at once onto wax paper, spread apart and cool completely. Break apart and store tightly covered.
notes: Orville Redenbacher credited this to his sister Mabel and called it the best caramel corn he ever tasted.

recipes.title: Fondant
steps: Place the sugar, water and cream of tartar in a pan and cook gently without stirring until it reaches soft ball stage.
Pour onto a plate and let cool.
Add the vanilla and knead until it becomes a white, creamy mass.
Let it ripen 24 hours before using.
notes: Use it to stuff dates or make chocolate mint patties.
flags: The card doesn't say when to add the vanilla; it's usually worked in during kneading.

recipes.title: Candied Walnuts
steps: Cook the sugar, liquid, corn syrup and salt to soft ball stage.
Add the walnuts and stir until creamy.
Turn out on waxed paper and separate with a fork.
notes: Orange: use 1/2 cup orange juice and 6 drops orange coloring.
Mint: use 1/2 cup milk, 4 drops red coloring and 1 tsp. peppermint flavoring.

recipes.title: Candy Corn (Candied Popcorn)
steps: Mix the sugar, butter and water in a saucepan.
Boil without stirring until threads form on the spoon when lifted.
Pour over the popcorn and stir until it's all coated.
notes: It's sugar-glazed popcorn, not the Halloween candy. Recipe from "(paper)."

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cups (Bars)
steps: Beat the powdered sugar into the soft margarine.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs and peanut butter, and press into a 9x13 pan.
Melt the chocolate chips and spread over the mixture.
Cut before the chocolate cools completely (about 30 to 60 minutes).
notes: No-bake bars that taste like peanut butter cups.
flags: "1 package" of graham crackers is probably one sleeve, about 1 1/2 cups crumbs.

recipes.title: Panocha
steps: Melt the butter and spread it over the sides of the pan.
Pour in the milk and bring to a boil.
Add the sugars and dissolve. Cover and bring to a boil slowly, about 1 minute, until the sugar crystals melt off the sides of the pan.
Uncover and continue a gentle boil, stirring, to soft ball stage, 238° (about 20 minutes).
Remove from heat and cool to lukewarm, about 1 hour.
Add the vanilla and nuts and stir with a heavy spoon until creamy and it starts to lose its gloss.
Pour into a buttered pan and cut while still warm.
notes: Marked "good." Panocha is brown-sugar fudge.
flags: No pan size given; an 8x8 buttered pan is typical.

recipes.title: Peanutty Caramel Corn
ingredients: 1 to 2 cups peanuts or other nuts
steps: Sort out the unpopped kernels and measure the popped corn into a large bowl.
Combine the sugars, corn syrup, water, vinegar and salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Heat to boiling over medium-high heat, stirring often.
Cook, stirring constantly, to 260° (hard ball stage).
Reduce heat to low and stir in the butter until melted. Add the peanuts and stir to coat.
Pour the syrup in a thin stream over the popcorn, stirring until well coated.
Spread on a 12x15 1/2-inch baking sheet. Cool and break into pieces.

recipes.title: Jean's Tuna Macaroni Salad
steps: Boil the macaroni. When it's done, rinse it, then cover it with cold water until the macaroni is cold. Drain.
Add the tuna, peas, cheese and onion and mix in.
Add the mayonnaise and Miracle Whip, and the yellow and Dijon mustard (about as much as you'd put on 2 hot dogs).
Sprinkle Mrs. Dash over the whole bowl and mix.
Add more mustard, seasoning and Miracle Whip until it tastes right.
notes: From an email by Jean Jones, William's mom, which William forwarded to his daughter in July 2019.
In her words: "I just play with it till it tastes right. Hope it turns out."

recipes.title: Ranch Pork Chops or Chicken

photos.label: The note (shared with the 4 Layer Dip)

ingredients: Chicken broth, enough to cover the meat
steps: Put the meat in the slow cooker with the soup, stock and ranch seasoning.
Add enough chicken broth to cover the meat.
Cook on low 4 to 8 hours, or on high for 4 hours.
notes: In Tammy's handwriting.
No title on the note; named here from the ingredients.
Written on a notepad page; the 4 Layer Dip is on the same sheet.
flags: A word before "stock" is scribbled out (maybe "broth").
The low-setting time reads "4 8 hours"; could be 4 to 8 or 6 to 8.
The note never says slow cooker, but "cook on low / on high" points to one.

recipes.title: 4 Layer Dip

photos.label: The note (shared with Ranch Pork Chops)

steps: Mix the Miracle Whip, sour cream and taco seasoning. Put in the fridge overnight.
Layer in a dish: bean dip, the sour cream mixture, salsa, then cheddar cheese on top.
notes: In Tammy's handwriting.
Written on the same sheet as the pork chop recipe.
flags: The note doesn't give the layer order; bean dip, cream, salsa, cheese is the usual one.
The bean dip, salsa and cheese are listed a few lines below the dip, so they may have been meant as a separate list.

recipes.title: Italian Meat Loaf
recipes.format: Printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, front and back
steps: Combine the meat, egg, cracker crumbs, onion, the 1/3 cup tomato sauce, salt, oregano and pepper.
Shape into a 10" x 12" rectangle on waxed paper. Sprinkle with the cheese.
Roll up and press the ends to seal. Place in a shallow pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Pour the 2/3 cup sauce over the top and bake another 15 minutes.
notes: A rolled meat loaf with mozzarella spiraled through the middle.
flags: Contributor's last name is hard to read: "Lao", "Loo" or "Leo".

recipes.title: Oven-Fried Chicken
recipes.format: Newspaper clipping on a lined card
steps: Mix the egg and milk. Dip each piece of chicken in it, then in the crumbs mixed with the seasonings.
Let stand about 20 minutes to dry the coating.
Melt the butter in a shallow baking dish. Arrange the chicken skin side down in a single layer.
Bake at 375° about 40 minutes, turn, and bake about 20 minutes more until golden brown and tender.
notes: The title is handwritten above the pasted clipping.
Accent is a brand of MSG seasoning.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Beef Stew
recipes.contributor: Dawn Robson of La Jolla, California
ingredients: 1 16-ounce can pork and beans in tomato sauce
steps: In a skillet, cook the ground beef and onion until the meat is browned and the onion tender; drain.
Add the remaining ingredients. Bring to boiling, then reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes or until heated through.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Beef N' Beans
steps: Brown the beef and onion in a skillet; drain the fat and move to the slow cooker.
Add the other ingredients and stir to mix.
Cover and cook on low 4 to 5 hours.

recipes.title: Spanish Omelet
ingredients: 1 ounce cheese (Swiss, Edam or your choice)
steps: Mix the first five ingredients and cook in a Teflon fry pan, as for a cheese omelet.
Top with warm stewed tomatoes.
notes: Diabetic exchanges: 2 meat, 1 vegetable, 2 fat.
Refers to a "cheese omelet" card from the same set that isn't in the box so far.

recipes.title: Meat with Dumplings
ingredients: Meatballs: 1 lb ground meat, 1/2 tsp salt
Thickener: 3 tbsp flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/4 cup cold water
Dumplings: 1 cup flour, 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, 2 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 1/4 tsp salt, 3/4 cup milk
steps: Mix the meat and salt, form small balls and pan fry.
Pan fry the onions and celery.
Add the potatoes and tomatoes and cook until done.
Make a paste of the flour, salt, pepper and cold water and stir it into the vegetables.
Add the meatballs and cook until thickened.
For the dumplings, mix the flours, baking powder and salt, then add the milk.
Drop the dumplings onto the stew, cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes.
notes: Brackets on the card group the ingredients into steps.
flags: A word before "Flour" in the dumplings is blotted out.
The dumpling salt may read 1 1/4 or 1/4 tsp (the fraction is written over).
The card says only "add dumplings"; dropping by spoonfuls is assumed.

recipes.title: Stadium Chicken Dogs
ingredients: Toppings: ketchup, mustard, relish, chopped onion, shredded cheese, chili with beans, or any favorites
steps: Prepare the chicken as directed on the package.
Place the nuggets in the buns.
Top with any of the toppings.

recipes.title: Balsamic Glazed Chicken
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Preheat oven to 425°.
In a large bowl, combine the balsamic, honey, mustard and garlic. Season with salt and pepper and stir until combined.
Add the chicken and toss until fully covered. Marinate in the fridge 20 minutes up to an hour.
Cut the potatoes. Season with salt, pepper and rosemary, plus 1 tbsp olive oil.
In a large skillet, sear the chicken in the remaining olive oil, 2 minutes each side.
Add the potato mixture to the skillet with the chicken.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the chicken is tender. Serve with the pan drippings.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
"20 min or so" is squeezed in above the baking line.
flags: The olive oil amount for the potatoes is written over; 1 tbsp is the best reading.

recipes.title: Original Ranch Crispy Chicken
ingredients: 1 packet Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing & Seasoning Mix
1 cup unseasoned dry bread crumbs (or cornflake crumbs)
1 roasting chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into 8 pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Combine the seasoning mix and bread crumbs in a gallon-size food storage bag.
Add the chicken pieces, seal, and shake to coat evenly.
Bake on an ungreased pan at 375°F for 50 minutes, or until the juices run clear or it reaches 165°F inside.

recipes.title: Egg Rolls
steps: No directions on the note, just the shopping list.
notes: In Tammy's handwriting.
flags: "C.B." isn't spelled out; cabbage or coleslaw blend is the likely meaning.
No amounts or directions.

recipes.title: Fiesta Chicken Empanada
ingredients: 1 (15-oz.) pkg. Pillsbury refrigerated pie crusts, softened as directed
1/2 medium red bell pepper, cut into 2x1/4-inch strips
1/2 medium green bell pepper, cut into strips
1/2 medium yellow bell pepper, cut into strips
1 (10-oz.) can chunk white chicken breast in water, drained
1/2 cup Old El Paso Cheese 'n Salsa Dip
Garnish if desired: sour cream, more Cheese 'n Salsa Dip
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Unfold the crusts and press out the fold lines. Place 1 crust on an ungreased 14-inch pizza pan or cookie sheet.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and peppers 5 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally. Add the chicken and fajita seasoning; mix well.

Spoon the chicken mixture onto the crust to within 1 inch of the edge. Spread the 1/2 cup dip over it. Brush the edge with water, top with the second crust, and press the edges firmly to seal. Brush the top with egg.
Bake at 425°F 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden brown, covering the edge with foil after 10 to 15 minutes. Cut into wedges and garnish.

recipes.title: Flaky Deli Slices
ingredients: 1 (15-oz.) pkg. Pillsbury refrigerated pie crusts, softened as directed
3/4 lb. very thinly sliced cooked ham
steps: Heat oven to 450°F. Unfold the crusts, press out the fold lines, and sprinkle each with Parmesan.
Top each crust with ham, pepperoni and Cheddar to within 1 inch of the edges. Roll up loosely and place seam side down on an ungreased cookie sheet. Fold the ends under.
Bake 12 to 17 minutes until golden brown. Cool 5 minutes, cut each roll into 16 slices, and serve warm.

recipes.title: Original Ranch Roasted Potatoes
ingredients: 1 packet Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing & Seasoning Mix
steps: Put the potatoes and oil in a gallon-size food storage bag, seal, and toss to coat.
Add the seasoning mix and toss again until coated.
Bake on an ungreased pan at 450°F for 30 to 35 minutes, until brown and crisp.

recipes.title: Sloppy Joe Casserole
steps: Brown the ground beef and mix with the Manwich sauce.
Line a baking dish with crescent dough. Add a layer of the Manwich mixture and sprinkle half the cheese over the top.
Repeat the layers.
Bake at the temperature and time on the crescent roll package.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The card doesn't say to brown the beef; that step is filled in.

recipes.title: Classic Italian Meatballs
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Mix the meatball ingredients and roll into balls.
Cook entirely on high.
Heat up the sauce and spoon it over the meatballs.
Sprinkle Parmesan over the top.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
A big batch: 4 1/2 pounds of meat.
flags: The bread crumb unit is written over; cups is the likely reading.
"Cook entirely on high" doesn't say slow cooker or stovetop.
Unclear whether all the Parmesan goes in the meatballs or some is saved for the top.

recipes.title: Orange Marmalade & BBQ Chicken
ingredients: 3/4 cup Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce
steps: Mix the marmalade, BBQ sauce and soy sauce into a marinade.
Cover the chicken with the marinade in a pan and cook on high until the chicken is no longer pink inside.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The marmalade and BBQ sauce amounts say just "3/4"; cups assumed.

recipes.title: Sweet Hawaiian Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 red pepper, chopped in tiny bits
1/2 green pepper, chopped in tiny bits
steps: Cook everything in a skillet until the chicken is cooked thoroughly.
Serve with white or brown rice.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: "Slice" before "tiny pineapple chunks" is unclear.

recipes.title: Stuffing Meat Loaf
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
steps: Preheat oven to 350°. Coat the pan with margarine.
Put the warm water, onion soup mix and stuffing in a bowl and mix well. Let sit 5 minutes for the bread to absorb the water.
Add the eggs and ground beef. It works best if you mix with your hands.
Place in the dish. Bake 1 hour or until no longer pink inside.
Let sit 5 minutes before serving.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: Hawaiian Beef
steps: Shake the meat strips in the flour, salt and pepper.
Arrange in a casserole and put the onions on top.
Mix the catsup, vinegar, Worcestershire, soy sauce, sugar and water and pour over the meat.
Cover and bake at 300° for 3 hours. Serve with rice.
notes: Credited to Ann Caldwell, who also gave the Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cake (No. 046).
flags: The sugar line says just "1/2"; cup assumed.

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 2 lbs. chicken, thinly sliced (1 inch across)
steps: Cook everything in a skillet until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Serve with white or brown rice. Drizzle extra sauce over the rice if desired.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The first line doesn't name the meat; chicken from the title.

recipes.title: Porcupines
recipes.format: Printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, front and back
steps: Mix the beef, onion, egg, salts and rice and form into balls.
Simmer the tomato soup and water, and add the meatballs.
Cook slowly (maybe 1/2 hour?), but check the meat to see if it is done.
notes: Spelled "Porkipines" on the card, with "(grnd beef)" written above.
The cook's own question mark is on the back: "maybe 1/2 hr?"
flags: Uncooked rice is usual for porcupine meatballs and usually needs closer to an hour to soften.

recipes.title: Lasagne
recipes.format: Printed "Here's what's cookin'" card, front and back
ingredients: Meat sauce: 1 lb. ground beef, 1 garlic clove, 1 T parsley, 1 T basil, 1/2 t salt, 1 lb. can tomatoes, 12 oz. can tomato paste
Cheese mixture: 3 c. cottage cheese, 2 T parsley, 2 beaten eggs, 1/2 c. Parmesan cheese, 2 tsp. salt, 1/2 tsp. pepper
steps: Brown the beef in a skillet. Add the garlic, parsley, basil, salt, tomatoes and tomato paste and simmer 30 minutes.
Combine the cheese mixture ingredients.
Cook the noodles.
In a 13x9 pan, layer half the noodles, half the cheese mixture and half the meat mixture. Repeat.
Sprinkle with the mozzarella.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes, until the cheese melts, and serve.
notes: "Recipe from the kitchen of: V. Sharp" is Violet Sharp, Grandma Sharp herself.
"Serves 10-15" and "375° oven" are noted in the top corner.

recipes.title: Ground Chicken Stir Fry with Rice
steps: Prepare the vegetables and precook the rice; set aside.
Brown the chicken and drain well.
Mix all ingredients in a fry pan or wok and cook until the vegetables are crisp.
notes: Use any combination of vegetables you wish.
Goes with the Yoshida's sauce leaflet (No. 101).

recipes.title: Saucy Asian Meatballs
recipes.format: Handwritten striped card, front and back
ingredients: Meatballs: 2 lbs. ground beef, 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp sesame oil
1 tbsp olive oil, to grease the pan
1 tbsp sesame seeds, to sprinkle when done
Sauce: 1/3 cup hoisin sauce, 1/4 cup ketchup, 1/3 cup honey, 1/4 cup rice wine vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil
steps: Preheat oven to 400°. In a bowl, mix all the meatball ingredients except the olive oil.
Shape into balls. Grease the baking pan with the olive oil and place the meatballs in it.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes. While they cook, mix the sauce ingredients in a bowl.
When the meatballs are done, pour off all the liquid from the pan.
Pour the sauce over until the meatballs are completely covered. Sprinkle sesame seeds over the top.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).
flags: The rice wine vinegar says just "1/4"; cup assumed.

recipes.title: Tater Tot Casserole
steps: Preheat oven to 400°. Coat the bottom of the pan with margarine.
Cook the ground beef and onions, then drain the grease. Pour into the baking dish.
Spoon the soup over the mixture. Layer the Tater Tots over the soup.
Bake 45 minutes or until the tots are golden brown and the mixture is bubbling.
notes: One of Tammy's cards (the striped ones are hers).

recipes.title: Yoshida's Gourmet Sauce Recipes
recipes.contributor: Yoshida's (Oregon Trading Post Co., Beaverton, OR)
ingredients: Pork chops, salmon, ground round, or chicken (per recipe)
steps: Karate Chops: Brown pork chops in a little shortening and drain. Put in a casserole, brush with 2 to 4 tbsp sauce (crushed pineapple optional), and bake at 350° about 20 minutes. Turn, brush with more sauce, and bake about 20 minutes more.
Sayonara Salmon: Marinate salmon steaks or fillets in the sauce 1 hour. Broil or barbecue, basting with drippings. Garnish with parsley, sauteed onions or lemon.
Teriyaki Burgers: Mix 1/4 cup sauce and 1/4 cup chopped onion into 1 1/2 lbs. ground round. Shape patties and broil, barbecue or pan fry.

Gourmet Chicken: Use about 1/4 cup sauce per pound of chicken. Spoon over chicken pieces in a casserole and bake at 350° about 20 minutes. Turn, baste, and bake 25 minutes more. For skinless breasts, marinate 1 hour first.
Fried Chicken: Pour 2 oz. sauce into an electric fry pan at 250°. Add chicken and turn to coat. Cook covered, turning every 5 minutes, 20 to 25 minutes. Uncover for the last 5 minutes to glaze.
notes: The Fried Chicken recipe was typed onto the bottom of the leaflet by someone in the family.
The Ground Chicken Stir Fry (No. 098) uses the same sauce.

recipes.title: Tangy Chicken of the Islands
recipes.format: Clipping taped to a recipe card
ingredients: 1 (2 to 3 lb.) frying chicken, cut into serving pieces
steps: Put the vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and pepper in a skillet. Add the chicken and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Heat to boiling on top of the stove. Cover, lower heat, and simmer about 40 minutes; the liquid absorbs into the chicken.
Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Baked Beans
steps: Cook the bacon (and onion).
Cook all together.
notes: In Tammy's handwriting.
flags: The can count and size are written over: probably "2 28 oz. or 4 16 oz."
The last line ends "at 3" with a scribble; maybe 325° or 3 hours.
The Worcestershire amount is written over; 1 tablespoon is the likely reading.

recipes.title: Chinese Casserole
ingredients: 2/3 can water, or juice from the can of vegetables
steps: Mix everything together.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
notes: "Some diced onion" was added later in pencil.
flags: The water amount is written over; 2/3 can is the best reading.

recipes.title: Porcupines (Hamburger)
steps: Mix the meat, onion, egg, salts and rice and form into balls.
Simmer the tomato soup and water, and add the meatballs.
Serve with spaetzle (noodles).
notes: Spelled "Porkepines". Same recipe as No. 096 in different handwriting, with a serving tip: "real good with spätzle (noodles)."
See No. 096 for the cooking time ("maybe 1/2 hr? but check meat").
flags: A few words after "balls +" are crossed out.

recipes.title: Quick Skillet Beef and Dumplings
steps: Brown the beef and onion in a large skillet; pour off excess fat.
Add the tomato sauce, vegetables, water, salt, thyme and pepper. Combine well and bring to a boil.
Mix the biscuit mix, milk and Parmesan. Spoon over the boiling beef mixture in 5 to 6 mounds.
Lower heat and simmer uncovered 10 minutes, then cover and simmer another 10 minutes.
notes: The clipping's headline misspells it "Dumpings".
flags: The water amount is smudged; 2/3 cup is the likely reading.

recipes.title: Yummy Balls
ingredients: 1 can tomato soup, thinned with a little water
steps: Mix the meat, onion, rice, cracker crumbs, egg, salt and pepper well. Shape into balls.
Pile in a well-oiled casserole. Pour the tomato soup, thinned with a little water, over all.
Cover the casserole and bake about 1 hour "at any heat."
notes: Another cousin of the Porcupines (No. 096, 105), baked instead of simmered.
The card really does say "at any heat"; 350° is a safe choice.

recipes.title: Mexican Mac
ingredients: Optional toppings: sour cream or guacamole, and/or tortilla chips
steps: Brown the beef in a pan.
Mix the water and taco seasoning, add to the browned beef, and simmer 15 minutes.
Prepare the mac and cheese as directed on the package.
Fold the beef mixture and mac and cheese together and serve.
Top with sour cream or guacamole and/or tortilla chips if you like.
notes: Signed "Recipe from: Violet Sharp" — Grandma Sharp.

recipes.title: Stir-Fry Chicken
recipes.format: Printed recipe taped to a "Here's what's cookin'" card
steps: Cut the chicken into very thin slices; set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the broth, cornstarch and soy sauce. Set aside.
In a 10-inch skillet or wok over medium heat, add 2 T. oil and stir-fry the chicken until browned.
Add the remaining 1 T. oil. Add the broccoli and mushrooms and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry 30 seconds more.
Return the chicken to the skillet. Stir in the broth mixture, bring to a boil, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more. Spoon over rice.
notes: The title is handwritten on the card above the taped-on recipe.
